question: The central bank may _________ to discourage credit in the economy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is increase bank rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bank Rate is the rate at which the central bank (RBI) lends long-term funds to commercial banks without any collateral. (बैंक दर — साख का हतोत्साहन)

 

• To discourage/contract credit in the economy (a dear-money or contractionary policy), the central bank raises the bank rate, making borrowing costlier for commercial banks, which then raise their own lending rates and reduce credit creation.

 

• This is one of the quantitative credit control instruments used by RBI, along with CRR, SLR and open market operations (OMO), to regulate money supply and credit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bank Rate is governed under Section 49 of the RBI Act, 1934, and is currently kept aligned with the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate.

 

• Other key monetary policy tools include the Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).

 

NOTE

 

• Decrease CRR (Option 1): A decrease in Cash Reserve Ratio releases more funds with banks for lending, thereby increasing/encouraging credit, not discouraging it.

 

• Buy securities in open market (Option 2): When the central bank buys securities, it injects money into the banking system, which increases credit availability — an expansionary, not contractionary, measure.

 

• Reduce SLR (Option 3): A reduction in Statutory Liquidity Ratio frees up more funds for banks to lend, thereby increasing credit in the economy.

question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?
option_1: Safeguard public property and abjure violence
option_2: Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
option_4: Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Exercise adult franchise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties are listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मूल कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• Exercising adult franchise (the right to vote) is not listed among the Fundamental Duties; it is a right/facility available to every citizen above 18 years of age under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, not a duty under Article 51A.

 

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were incorporated; an 11th duty — the duty of parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to children between 6-14 years — was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they cannot be directly enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

• The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

NOTE

 

• Safeguard public property and abjure violence (Option 1): This is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(i).

 

• Cherish and follow the noble ideals of the freedom struggle (Option 2): This is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(b).

 

• Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (Option 4): This is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(c).

question: Which festival has the meaning ‘to boil’ or ‘boiling’ in its name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pongal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pongal is a Tamil harvest festival, and the word itself literally means "to boil over" / "boiling", referring to the ritual of boiling freshly harvested rice with milk and jaggery until it overflows the pot, symbolising abundance. (पोंगल — 'उबलना' अर्थ)

 

• It is celebrated over four days in mid-January, coinciding with the Tamil month of Thai, and marks the sun's transition into the Makara (Capricorn) zodiac, similar to Makar Sankranti.

 

• The four days of the festival are named Bhogi Pongal, Surya Pongal (Thai Pongal), Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Makar Sankranti (North India), Lohri (Punjab) and Bihu (Assam) are other harvest festivals celebrated around mid-January.

 

NOTE

 

• Onam (Option 2): A harvest festival of Kerala celebrating the homecoming of the mythical King Mahabali; its name comes from the star Thiruvonam, not from 'boiling'.

 

• Raja (Option 3): A festival celebrated in Odisha marking the onset of the monsoon and celebrating womanhood, symbolised as the menstruation of Mother Earth (Bhudevi).

 

• Bihu (Option 4): The principal festival of Assam, celebrated thrice a year (Rongali/Bohag, Kongali/Kati and Bhogali/Magh Bihu), each marking a different agricultural phase.

question: Vitamins and minerals are helpful for which of the following?
option_4: Carry out metabolic reactions in our body
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carry out metabolic reactions in our body.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vitamins and minerals are essential micronutrients required by the body in small quantities to regulate and carry out metabolic reactions, acting as coenzymes and cofactors for the enzymes involved. (विटामिन एवं खनिज — उपापचय क्रियाएँ)

 

• Unlike carbohydrates, fats and proteins, vitamins and minerals do not themselves provide energy; instead, they help the body utilise energy-yielding nutrients efficiently.

 

• For example, B-complex vitamins (B1, B2, B3, etc.) act as coenzymes in carbohydrate and energy metabolism, while minerals like iron are essential for oxygen transport and cellular respiration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vitamins are classified as fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) and water-soluble (B-complex, C).

 

• Deficiency diseases include: Vitamin C deficiency → Scurvy, Vitamin D deficiency → Rickets, and Iron deficiency → Anaemia.

 

NOTE

 

• Proper breathing (Option 1): Breathing/respiration is primarily controlled by the respiratory system and the medulla oblongata, not directly by vitamins and minerals.

 

• Proper sweating (Option 2): Sweating is a thermoregulatory function controlled by the hypothalamus and sweat glands, not a principal role of vitamins/minerals.

 

• Proper fat storage (Option 3): Fat storage occurs mainly in adipose tissue and is regulated by hormones, not primarily by vitamins and minerals.

question:
Which of the following is the correct match of the column-A with column-B?

Column-A (Physical Property)

i. Electric current

ii. Voltage

iii. Capacitance

iv. Magnetic field

Column-B (Unit)

a. Tesla

b. Farad

c. Ampere

d. Volt
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), named after Andre-Marie Ampere. (विद्युत धारा की इकाई — एम्पियर)

 

• The SI unit of voltage (potential difference) is the Volt (V), named after Alessandro Volta.

 

• The SI unit of capacitance is the Farad (F), named after Michael Faraday.

 

• The SI unit of magnetic field (magnetic flux density) is the Tesla (T), named after Nikola Tesla.

 

• Matching correctly: i. Electric current → c. Ampere; ii. Voltage → d. Volt; iii. Capacitance → b. Farad; iv. Magnetic field → a. Tesla, which corresponds to i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistance is measured in Ohm (Ω), Power in Watt (W), and Energy/Work in Joule (J).

 

• Frequency is measured in Hertz (Hz) and Electric charge in Coulomb (C).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each of them mismatches at least one physical quantity with the wrong SI unit, as shown by the correct pairing above.

question: Emperor Ashoka conquered Kalinga after how many years of his coronation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ashoka was crowned emperor of the Mauryan Empire around 269 BCE, and the Kalinga War was fought in 261 BCE, i.e., 8 years after his coronation. (कलिंग युद्ध — राज्याभिषेक के 8 वर्ष बाद)

 

• The Kalinga War was fought against the independent kingdom of Kalinga (present-day coastal Odisha).

 

• The immense bloodshed and suffering witnessed in this war deeply affected Ashoka, leading to his conversion to Buddhism and adoption of the policy of "Dhamma" (moral governance).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Details of the Kalinga War and Ashoka's remorse are recorded in his Rock Edict XIII.

 

• Ashoka's edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837; most are written in Brahmi script and Prakrit language.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 years, 11 years and 15 years (Options 1, 3 and 4) are incorrect; historically, the Kalinga War is dated to about 8 years after Ashoka's coronation (c. 269 BCE coronation, 261 BCE war).

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that law declared by Supreme Court is binding on all courts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 141.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 141 of the Constitution of India states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. (अनुच्छेद 141 — सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के निर्णय सभी न्यायालयों पर बाध्यकारी)

 

• This provision establishes the doctrine of precedent (stare decisis) in the Indian judicial system, ensuring uniformity in the interpretation and application of law across the country.

 

• Article 141 falls under Part V of the Constitution, dealing with the Union Judiciary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 141 applies to all courts except the Supreme Court itself, which is not bound by its own previous decisions and can review/overrule them.

 

• The Supreme Court of India was established on 26 January 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 143 (Option 1): Deals with the power of the President to consult the Supreme Court on questions of law or fact of public importance (advisory jurisdiction).

 

• Article 142 (Option 2): Empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any matter pending before it.

 

• Article 144 (Option 3): Requires all civil and judicial authorities in India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.

question: Who became the first woman soldier sky diver of the Indian Army to have jumped from a height of 10,000 feet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lance Naik Manju.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lance Naik Manju became the Indian Army's first woman soldier sky diver, completing a jump from a height of 10,000 feet. (लांस नायक मंजू — प्रथम महिला स्काई डाइवर)

 

• She achieved this feat as part of the Army Adventure Wing/parachute training establishment, marking a milestone for women in combat-support and adventure roles in the Indian Army.

 

• This achievement is part of the broader trend of increasing participation of women soldiers in specialised and adventure activities within the Indian Armed Forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Army has progressively opened up combat and specialised roles to women, including as fighter pilots (IAF), naval officers on warships, and Corps of Engineers/Army Air Defence officers.

 

NOTE

 

• Lieutenant General Madhuri Kanitkar (Option 1): A senior Indian Army officer known for becoming one of the first women Lieutenant Generals and later Vice Chancellor of a health university; not associated with this skydiving feat.

 

• Lieutenant General Rajshree Ramasethu (Option 3): A distractor name, not associated with this skydiving achievement.

 

• Air Marshal Arti Sarin (Option 4): An Indian Air Force officer, notable as one of the first women Air Marshals in the IAF, unrelated to this Army skydiving record.

question: Who is known as the ‘Father of Modern Dance in India’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uday Shankar is widely regarded as the "Father of Modern Dance in India" for pioneering a new dance form that blended Indian classical traditions with Western theatrical and ballet techniques. (उदय शंकर — आधुनिक नृत्य के जनक)

 

• He founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre at Almora and created iconic productions that popularised Indian dance globally in the early-to-mid 20th century.

 

• He was the elder brother of the renowned sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uday Shankar was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna).

 

• His notable disciple/collaborator institutions helped shape modern Indian creative/contemporary dance, distinct from strictly classical forms like Bharatanatyam or Kathak.

 

NOTE

 

• Birju Maharaj (Option 2): A legendary exponent and doyen of the Kathak classical dance form (Lucknow gharana), not associated with founding modern dance.

 

• Gopi Krishna (Option 3): A well-known Kathak dancer and film actor-choreographer, not the founder of modern dance in India.

 

• Guru Bipin Singh (Option 4): Renowned for reviving and systematising Manipuri classical dance, not modern dance.

question: In 2019, a minor planet between Mars and Jupiter was named after whom among the following Indian musicians by the International Astronomical Union (IAU)?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Pt Hari Prasad Chaurasia
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pt Jasraj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2019, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) named a minor planet (asteroid), located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, after the legendary Hindustani classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj. (पंडित जसराज — क्षुद्रग्रह नामकरण)

 

• With this, Pandit Jasraj became the first Indian musician to have a minor planet named in his honour.

 

• Pandit Jasraj was a renowned exponent of the Mewati Gharana of Hindustani classical vocal music and a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Jasraj passed away on 17 August 2020 in the USA.

 

• He was honoured with major civilian and music awards including the Padma Vibhushan (2000) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

NOTE

 

• Pt Hari Prasad Chaurasia (Option 1): A renowned flute (bansuri) maestro; no minor planet has been named after him.

 

• Pt Ravi Shankar (Option 2): A legendary sitar maestro and Bharat Ratna recipient; not the musician honoured with this particular IAU naming.

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain (Option 3): A world-renowned tabla virtuoso; not associated with this asteroid naming.

question: Who was the first nationalist to give the theory of drain of wealth from India to England?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the "Grand Old Man of India", was the first nationalist to systematically propound the "Drain of Wealth" theory in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901). (धन-निष्कासन सिद्धांत — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• The theory argued that a substantial part of India's wealth was being transferred/drained to Britain without adequate economic or material return, through home charges, salaries/pensions of British officials, interest on debt, and profits repatriated by British enterprises.

 

• Naoroji used the "Net National Product" method to estimate the drain and highlight India's economic exploitation under colonial rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji was also the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892), representing the Liberal Party from Finsbury Central.

 

• He was a founding member and thrice President of the Indian National Congress (1886, 1893, 1906).

 

NOTE

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 1): Led India's freedom movement through non-violence and Satyagraha; not the originator of the Drain of Wealth theory.

 

• RC Dutt (Option 2): Romesh Chunder Dutt further developed and popularised the drain theory in his work "Economic History of India", but Naoroji was the first to propound it.

 

• SN Banerjee (Option 3): Surendranath Banerjee was a prominent moderate nationalist leader and founder of the Indian National Association, not associated with originating this theory.

question: Khemraj received the Sangeet Natak Akademi award for his contribution to folk music and dance of ‘Kud’. Which state is the folk dance from?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kud is a traditional folk dance of the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir, performed as a ritualistic dance to please local deities during harvest and festive occasions. (कूद नृत्य — जम्मू और कश्मीर)

 

• Khemraj was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to the folk music and dance form of Kud.

 

• The dance is typically performed at night around a bonfire, accompanied by instruments like the chhaina, narsingha and dhol.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Jammu and Kashmir include Rouf, Dumhal and Hikat.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, was established in 1952 and is the oldest of the national academies for arts in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Ghoomar and Phag, not Kud.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Nati and Rasa, not Kud.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Bhangra and Giddha, not Kud.

question: During Alauddin Khilji’s reign, the cloth market was known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarai-i-Adl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khilji introduced a comprehensive market control system to regulate prices, primarily to maintain a large and inexpensive standing army. (सराय-ए-अदल — कपड़ा बाजार)

 

• Under this system, the market for cloth and other high-value/imported goods was called the "Sarai-i-Adl" (meaning "place of justice/fair dealing"), located near the Badaun Gate in Delhi.

 

• The general food-grain market was called "Mandi", and prices there were fixed and monitored strictly by officials.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Officials appointed to enforce market regulations included the Shahna-i-Mandi (market controller) and spies called Munhiyans/Munhiyan who reported on prices and irregularities.

 

• Alauddin Khilji's market reforms are described in detail by the contemporary chronicler Ziauddin Barani in his work Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

 

NOTE

 

• Mandi (Option 2): This was the market for food grains, not cloth, under Alauddin Khilji's system.

 

• Munhiyans (Option 3): These were the secret informers/spies who reported on market prices and dealings to the Sultan, not a market name.

 

• Shahna-i-Mandi (Option 4): This was the title of the officer/controller in charge of the grain market (Mandi), not the name of the cloth market.

question: The Ryotwari Settlement, in which cultivators had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, was primarily introduced in which of the following provinces?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madras and Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ryotwari Settlement was a land revenue system introduced primarily in the Madras and Bombay Presidencies of British India. (रैयतवाड़ी व्यवस्था — मद्रास और बॉम्बे)

 

• Under this system, the land revenue settlement was made directly between the government and the individual cultivator (ryot), without intermediaries like zamindars, and the ryot had to pay taxes annually directly to the state.

 

• It was pioneered by Captain Alexander Read and later systematically implemented by Sir Thomas Munro (Governor of Madras).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Permanent (Zamindari) Settlement was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793, primarily in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and parts of Varanasi.

 

• The Mahalwari System was introduced in parts of the North-Western Provinces, Central Provinces and Punjab, where revenue settlement was made village/mahal-wise.

 

NOTE

 

• Central province (Option 1): This region was primarily under the Mahalwari system, not Ryotwari.

 

• Assam and Bengal (Option 2): Bengal was primarily under the Permanent (Zamindari) Settlement, not the Ryotwari system.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): This region was primarily under the Mahalwari system, not the Ryotwari system.

question: In which part of the Himalayas does its highest mountain peak, Kanchenjunga, lie?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanchenjunga, the highest peak in India and the third-highest mountain in the world (8,586 m), lies in the Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas, on the border between Sikkim (India) and Nepal. (कंचनजंगा — दार्जिलिंग एवं सिक्किम हिमालय)

 

• The Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas stretch between the Tista and Singalila ranges, forming part of the Eastern/Nepal Himalayan longitudinal division of the Great Himalayas.

 

• Kanchenjunga is regarded as a sacred peak by the local Sikkimese people and is worshipped as a guardian deity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mount Everest (8,849 m), the world's highest peak, lies in the Nepal Himalayas.

 

• The Himalayas are longitudinally divided into regions such as the Kashmir/Punjab Himalayas, Himachal-Uttarakhand (Kumaon) Himalayas, Darjeeling-Sikkim (Nepal) Himalayas, and Arunachal (Assam) Himalayas.

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Himalayas (Option 1): Located in the eastern-most part of India; Kangto is generally its highest peak, not Kanchenjunga.

 

• Kashmir Himalayas (Option 2): Home to peaks like Nanga Parbat (though geopolitically contested territory); Kanchenjunga does not lie here.

 

• Uttarakhand Himalayas (Option 4): Home to peaks like Nanda Devi, the second-highest peak in India; Kanchenjunga does not lie here.

question: As per the report released by NITI Aayog in September 2021 entitled ‘Best Practices in the Performance of District Hospitals’, on average, how many beds per lakh population do district hospitals have?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24 beds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NITI Aayog, in its September 2021 report titled "Best Practices in the Performance of District Hospitals", found that district hospitals in India have, on average, 24 beds per lakh population. (जिला अस्पताल — प्रति लाख जनसंख्या 24 बेड)

 

• The report assessed the performance of 707 district hospitals across states/UTs based on a set of health indicators and infrastructure parameters.

 

• The study aimed to identify best practices to strengthen district-level healthcare infrastructure, especially highlighted by the gaps exposed during the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was formed in January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

 

• NITI Aayog also releases other important indices such as the SDG India Index and the Health Index (ranking states on health outcomes).

 

NOTE

 

• 12 beds, 40 beds and 36 beds (Options 1, 2 and 4) are incorrect figures; the report's finding was an average of 24 beds per lakh population.

question: In which year was the ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana’ launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was launched in 2015 as the flagship skill development scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). (प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना — 2015)

 

• Its objective is to enable a large number of Indian youth to take up industry-relevant skill training to help them secure a better livelihood, with monetary rewards on successful completion.

 

• The scheme is implemented through the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMKVY 2.0 was launched for the period 2016-2020, and PMKVY 3.0 was launched in 2021.

 

• The Skill India Mission was also launched in 2015 under which PMKVY operates.

 

NOTE

 

• 2019, 2014 and 2020 (Options 1, 3 and 4) are incorrect; PMKVY was launched in 2015, though later phases were rolled out in subsequent years.

question: Which country hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qatar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 was hosted by Qatar, making it the first World Cup held in the Arab world/Middle East and the first held in a predominantly Muslim-majority country. (फीफा विश्व कप 2022 — कतर)

 

• It was also the first World Cup held in the winter season (November-December) rather than the traditional June-July slot, due to Qatar's extreme summer heat.

 

• Argentina won the tournament, defeating France in the final on penalties, with Lionel Messi lifting the trophy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The final was held at the Lusail Stadium, Qatar; the tournament mascot was La'eeb.

 

• The FIFA World Cup 2026 is scheduled to be jointly hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico.

 

NOTE

 

• Japan (Option 1): Co-hosted the FIFA World Cup 2002 with South Korea, not the 2022 edition.

 

• France (Option 3): Was the runner-up of the 2022 World Cup and had earlier hosted the tournament in 1998, not in 2022.

 

• USA (Option 4): Hosted the FIFA World Cup 1994 and is a co-host for 2026, not 2022.

question: In the early 1800s, who discovered that each chemical element is made up of a unique type of atom and that atoms differ by their mass?
solution_text:
The correct answer is John Dalton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• John Dalton, an English chemist, proposed the Atomic Theory of Matter in the early 1800s (1803-1808), stating that all matter is made of indivisible atoms and that atoms of a given element are identical, while atoms of different elements differ in mass and properties. (जॉन डाल्टन — परमाणु सिद्धांत)

 

• His theory was published in detail in his work "A New System of Chemical Philosophy" (1808).

 

• Dalton's postulates laid the foundation of modern chemistry, explaining the laws of chemical combination such as the Law of Conservation of Mass and Law of Definite Proportions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dalton is also known for his work on colour blindness, a condition once called "Daltonism" after him, as he himself was colour blind.

 

• Later scientific developments (e.g., discovery of electrons, protons, neutrons and isotopes) modified/refined Dalton's original atomic theory.

 

NOTE

 

• Antoine Lavoisier (Option 1): Known as the "Father of Modern Chemistry", credited with the Law of Conservation of Mass, not the atomic theory of distinct atomic masses.

 

• Amedeo Avogadro (Option 3): Proposed Avogadro's Law (equal volumes of gases at the same temperature/pressure contain equal numbers of molecules) in 1811, distinct from Dalton's atomic theory.

 

• Robert Boyle (Option 4): Known for Boyle's Law relating gas pressure and volume; considered a founder of modern chemistry but not the proposer of this atomic theory.

question:
Match the columns.

Column-A (Disorder)

i. Addison’s disease

ii. Hashimoto’s disease

iii. Acromegaly

iv. SIADH

Column-B (Hormone/Gland)

a. Adrenal gland

b. Thyroid gland

c. Growth hormone

d. Vasopressin
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Addison's disease is a disorder of the adrenal gland, caused by insufficient production of cortisol and aldosterone due to adrenal cortex damage. (एडिसन रोग — अधिवृक्क ग्रंथि)

 

• Hashimoto's disease is an autoimmune disorder of the thyroid gland, leading to chronic inflammation and hypothyroidism.

 

• Acromegaly is caused by excess growth hormone secretion (usually from a pituitary tumour) in adults after bone growth plates have closed.

 

• SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone secretion) results from excess secretion of vasopressin (ADH), causing the body to retain too much water.

 

• Matching correctly: i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The adrenal gland also secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline from its medulla, in addition to corticosteroids from its cortex.

 

• The pituitary gland, often called the "master gland", secretes growth hormone, ADH (via posterior pituitary) and several other regulatory hormones.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because each mismatches at least one disorder with the wrong gland/hormone, unlike the correct pairing in Option 3.

question: As of April 2022, who among the following is the Chairman of the National Green Tribunal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adarsh Kumar Goel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Adarsh Kumar Goel, a former judge of the Supreme Court of India, was appointed as the Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) in December 2018 and continued to hold the position as of April 2022. (न्यायमूर्ति आदर्श कुमार गोयल — राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण अध्यक्ष)

 

• The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection.

 

• The NGT's principal bench is located in New Delhi, with additional benches in Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NGT follows principles of natural justice and is not bound by the strict procedure of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.

 

• India became the third country (after Australia and New Zealand) to set up a specialised environmental tribunal.

 

NOTE

 

• Uday Umesh Lalit (Option 2): Served as the 49th Chief Justice of India (August-November 2022), not Chairman of NGT.

 

• Anoop Kumar Mendiratta (Option 3): Served as the Union Law Secretary, not NGT Chairman.

 

• Vikram Nath (Option 4): A judge of the Supreme Court of India, not associated with the NGT chairmanship.

question: Which of the following sedimentary minerals, known to everyone as ‘salt’, usually forms in arid climates where sea water evaporates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Halite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Halite, commonly known as rock salt (chemically sodium chloride, NaCl), is a sedimentary evaporite mineral that forms when saline water (such as seawater) evaporates in arid/dry climatic conditions, leaving behind mineral deposits. (हैलाइट — साधारण नमक)

 

• Halite deposits are typically found in playas, salt lakes, and marine basins in hot, dry regions where evaporation rates exceed water inflow.

 

• It commonly crystallises in a cubic crystal system and is colourless or white when pure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common evaporite minerals include gypsum (calcium sulphate) and sylvite (potassium chloride).

 

• India's largest salt-producing states include Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan (notably the Rann of Kutch and Sambhar Lake).

 

NOTE

 

• Zeolite (Option 1): A group of hydrated aluminosilicate minerals, often used as molecular sieves/catalysts, not the common salt mineral.

 

• Calcite (Option 3): A carbonate mineral (calcium carbonate, CaCO3), the primary constituent of limestone and marble, not table salt.

 

• Pyrite (Option 4): An iron sulphide mineral (FeS2), known as "fool's gold" due to its metallic lustre, not related to common salt.

question:
Which of the following modern industries was in operation in India during the British rule?

a. Cotton

b. Jute

c. Iron and Steel
option_1: All of a, b and c
solution_text:
The correct answer is All of a, b and c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During British rule, India saw the emergence of several modern, large-scale industries, including cotton textiles, jute, and iron and steel. (आधुनिक उद्योग — कपास, जूट, लोहा-इस्पात)

 

• The first modern cotton textile mill was established in Bombay in 1854 by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar; Bombay and Ahmedabad became major centres of the cotton textile industry.

 

• The first jute mill was set up near Kolkata (Rishra) in 1855, and the jute industry became concentrated largely in Bengal, dominated initially by British capital.

 

• The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established by Jamsetji Tata at Jamshedpur in 1907, marking the beginning of modern iron and steel production in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other industries that developed during colonial rule included coal mining, tea and coffee plantations, and paper industries.

 

• Indian-owned industrial enterprises like TISCO emerged as symbols of Swadeshi industrial enterprise alongside dominant British-owned industries.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each excludes at least one of the three industries (cotton, jute, iron and steel) that were genuinely operational during British rule.

question: Which of the following ports is NOT situated on the west coast of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haldia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Haldia port, located in West Bengal on the Hooghly river, is situated on the east coast of India, not the west coast. (हल्दिया बंदरगाह — पूर्वी तट)

 

• Mangaluru (New Mangalore Port) in Karnataka, Kandla (Deendayal Port) in Gujarat, and Marmagao Port in Goa are all major ports situated along India's west coast.

 

• India's west coast ports handle significant trade with the Middle East, Europe and Africa, given their geographic orientation towards the Arabian Sea.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has 12 major ports, including Kandla (Deendayal), Mumbai, JNPT (Nhava Sheva), Mormugao, New Mangalore and Cochin on the west coast, and Kolkata, Paradip, Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Ennore (Kamarajar) and V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) on the east coast.

 

• Kandla Port (renamed Deendayal Port) was developed after independence to compensate for the loss of Karachi port to Pakistan.

 

NOTE

 

• Mangaluru (Option 1): Located in Karnataka, on the west coast.

 

• Kandla (Option 2): Located in Gujarat, on the west coast.

 

• Marmagao (Option 3): Located in Goa, on the west coast.
